title: Experiment runners
blurb: The GPU runs of each experiment.

blocks.lead: Judge the main students at nine token budgets, from 10 to 8,192.

about.html: Shows whether accuracy changes gradually between the quick (10-token) and the reasoned (8,192-token) verdict or jumps at some budget. Each judge is loaded once and JudgeModel.evaluate_batch is called with every budget in turn, exactly as scripts/run_judge.py calls it for 10 and 8,192. The package picks the prompt and the thinking mode from the budget: PROMPT_QUICK at 10 tokens and PROMPT_REASONED above it, with thinking on only at 8,192. Judges with always_thinks skip the 10-token budget.

After each file the script logs its accuracy and instruction-following rate, computed by JudgeEvaluator, and at the end it prints a judge x dataset x budget table averaged over the students. Existing files are read instead of re-judged unless --force is given; a file that does not parse is judged again.
Reads results/core/student_solutions/<student>/<dataset>.json Writes results/token_budget/budget_sweep/<judge>/<student>_<dataset>_b<budget>.json
examples, from the repository root: python experiments/token_budget/run_budget_sweep.py --judges qwen3-8b python experiments/token_budget/run_budget_sweep.py --judges phi4-14b --tp 2 --gpu-mem 0.85
experiments/token_budget/analyze.py and experiments/adaptive_budget/analyze.py read the sweep.

python experiments/token_budget/run_budget_sweep.py [--judges JUDGES [JUDGES ...]] \

blocks.lead: Single-factor study: split the 10 -> 8,192-token accuracy change into its causes.

about.html: The quick and the reasoned verdict differ in more than the budget. At 10 tokens the package uses PROMPT_QUICK, greedy decoding and no thinking; at 8,192 it uses PROMPT_REASONED, and judges with enable_thinking also think and sample at temperature 0.6. Each factor condition below starts from the 10-token baseline and changes one of these, through the prompt_style, thinking and temperature arguments of JudgeModel.evaluate_batch:

about.code:
condition            budget  prompt    thinking  temperature
baseline_t10            10   (auto)    (auto)    (auto)       as scripts/run_judge.py
baseline_t8192        8192   (auto)    (auto)    (auto)       as scripts/run_judge.py
factor_budget         8192   quick     off       0
factor_prompt           10   reasoned  off       0
factor_thinking       8192   quick     on        0.6
factor_temperature      10   quick     off       0.6

about.html: The two baselines call evaluate_batch with the budget only, so they match the package's own runs. thinking=True turns thinking on only for judges whose config enables it. Judges with always_thinks have no 10-token configuration, so they skip baseline_t10, factor_prompt and factor_temperature.

Existing files are read instead of re-judged unless --force is given; a file that does not parse is judged again. At the end the script prints, per dataset, each condition's accuracy and its change from baseline_t10.
Reads results/core/student_solutions/<student>/<dataset>.json Writes results/token_budget/single_factor/<judge>/<condition>/<student>_<dataset>.json

examples, from the repository root: python experiments/token_budget/run_single_factor.py --judges qwen3-8b --factor all python experiments/token_budget/run_single_factor.py --judges qwen3-8b --factor thinking
experiments/token_budget/analyze.py reads the results.

    [--factor {all,baselines,budget,prompt,thinking,temperature}] \

    [--output-dir OUTPUT_DIR] [--force] \
    [--tensor-parallel-size TENSOR_PARALLEL_SIZE] \
    [--gpu-memory-utilization GPU_MEMORY_UTILIZATION] \
    [--max-num-seqs MAX_NUM_SEQS]

blocks.lead: Run a judge with one reworded prompt from slmjury/configs/prompt_variants.yaml.

about.html: The judge, students, items, sampling and verdict parsing are the same as in scripts/run_judge.py and scripts/run_scoring_judge.py. Only the prompt text changes. The variant is passed to the package through the optional prompt_template argument of JudgeModel.evaluate_batch, ScoringJudge.score_summeval and ScoringJudge.score_mtbench. The original variant passes nothing, so it runs the package's default prompts.

about.code:
Two prompt types:
  verdict   closed-ended; the "quick" text is used at 10 tokens and the
            "reasoned" text at 8,192, as the package chooses between
            PROMPT_QUICK and PROMPT_REASONED. Judges with always_thinks
            skip 10 tokens.
  scoring   SummEval and MT-Bench, scored against every reference-model file
            under --reference-scores (layout <reference>/<student>.json)

about.html: Existing files are skipped unless --force is given.

examples, from the repository root: python experiments/prompt_sensitivity/run_prompt_variants.py \ --judge qwen3-4b --variant minimal --max-tokens 10 8192 python experiments/prompt_sensitivity/run_prompt_variants.py \ --judge qwen3-4b --variant minimal --prompt-type scoring --max-tokens 8192

blocks.usage:
python experiments/prompt_sensitivity/run_prompt_variants.py --judge JUDGE \
    --variant \
    {original,minimal,gpt_style,rubric_based,cot_style,adversarial,few_shot} \
    [--prompt-type {verdict,scoring}] \
    [--max-tokens MAX_TOKENS [MAX_TOKENS ...]] \
    [--datasets DATASETS [DATASETS ...]] [--solutions-dir SOLUTIONS_DIR] \
    [--reference-scores REFERENCE_SCORES] [--output-dir OUTPUT_DIR] \
    [--force] [--tensor-parallel-size TENSOR_PARALLEL_SIZE] \
    [--gpu-memory-utilization GPU_MEMORY_UTILIZATION] \

blocks.lead: G-Eval-style judging: a score from 1 to 10, where 7 or more counts as Correct.

about.html: Same as scripts/run_judge.py except for the prompt and the verdict. PROMPT_GEVAL still shows the ground truth but asks for a rubric score instead of a verdict. It is passed to JudgeModel.evaluate_batch through prompt_template at every budget. Each response is then read with slmjury.parsers.score.parse_score on a 1-10 scale and thresholded; a response with no score is Undefined. Model loading and sampling are the package's. Judges with always_thinks skip 10 tokens. The default budget is 8,192 only, since a rubric score needs room to reason.

The judge is looked up in judge_models and then large_judge_models in slmjury/configs/models.yaml, so the same command runs small and large judges. Datasets are visited in the order of datasets_order.py. Existing files are skipped unless --force is given.

Reads --solutions-dir/<student>/<dataset>.json (default results/core/student_solutions) Writes --output-dir/<judge>/<student>_<dataset>_t<budget>.json (default results/judging_protocols/geval). Each record has the usual judgement fields plus numeric_score and threshold.
example, from the repository root: python experiments/judging_protocols/run_geval.py --judge qwen3-4b --max-tokens 8192
experiments/judging_protocols/analyze.py reads the results.

blocks.usage:
python experiments/judging_protocols/run_geval.py --judge JUDGE \
    [--max-tokens MAX_TOKENS [MAX_TOKENS ...]] [--threshold THRESHOLD] \
    [--solutions-dir SOLUTIONS_DIR] [--output-dir OUTPUT_DIR] [--force] \
    [--datasets [DATASETS ...]] [--exclude-datasets [EXCLUDE_DATASETS ...]] \
    [--tensor-parallel-size TENSOR_PARALLEL_SIZE] \
    [--gpu-memory-utilization GPU_MEMORY_UTILIZATION] \
    [--max-num-seqs MAX_NUM_SEQS]

blocks.lead: Pairwise judging in both answer orders, to measure position bias.

about.html: The judge sees one question, its ground truth and two students' answers, and answers "A" or "B" for the more correct one. Every pair is judged twice: in the forward run student a's answer is A, in the reverse run it is B. A judge without position bias picks the same student both times; the share of items where its pick follows the position instead is the flip rate.

PROMPT_PAIRWISE is filled in here and passed through JudgeModel.evaluate_batch with the template "{student_answer}", which forwards the filled prompt unchanged, so model loading and sampling are the package's. The choice is read from each response with slmjury.analysis.pairwise.read_choice. Judges with always_thinks skip 10 tokens.

By default every ordered pair of students (a, b) with a != b is run, which gives both "a_vs_b" and "b_vs_a" files. --unordered-pairs runs each pair once. Because (a, b) reversed shows the answers in the same order as (b, a) forward, this halves the cost and loses no prompt.

The judge is looked up in judge_models and then large_judge_models in slmjury/configs/models.yaml, so the same command runs small and large judges. Datasets are visited in the order of datasets_order.py. A pair is skipped when both of its files exist, unless --force is given.

Reads --solutions-dir/<student>/<dataset>.json (default results/core/student_solutions) Writes --output-dir/<judge>/<a>_vs_<b>_<dataset>_t<budget>_{fwd,rev}.json (default results/judging_protocols/pairwise)
example, from the repository root: python experiments/judging_protocols/run_pairwise.py --judge qwen3-4b --max-tokens 10 8192
experiments/judging_protocols/analyze.py reads the results.

blocks.usage:
python experiments/judging_protocols/run_pairwise.py --judge JUDGE \
    [--max-tokens MAX_TOKENS [MAX_TOKENS ...]] \
    [--solutions-dir SOLUTIONS_DIR] [--output-dir OUTPUT_DIR] [--force] \
    [--datasets [DATASETS ...]] [--exclude-datasets [EXCLUDE_DATASETS ...]] \
    [--unordered-pairs] [--tensor-parallel-size TENSOR_PARALLEL_SIZE] \
    [--gpu-memory-utilization GPU_MEMORY_UTILIZATION] \
    [--max-num-seqs MAX_NUM_SEQS]

blocks.lead: Judge the students without showing the judge the ground truth.

about.html: Same as scripts/run_judge.py except for the prompt. PROMPT_REFERENCEFREE_QUICK and PROMPT_REFERENCEFREE_REASONED are PROMPT_QUICK and PROMPT_REASONED with the ground-truth line removed and the instructions reworded to match. They are passed to JudgeModel.evaluate_batch through prompt_template: the quick text at 10 tokens and the reasoned text otherwise, the same way the package chooses its own prompts. Model loading, sampling, verdict parsing and the output format are the package's. Judges with always_thinks skip 10 tokens.

The judge is looked up in judge_models and then large_judge_models in slmjury/configs/models.yaml, so the same command runs small and large judges. Datasets are visited in the order of datasets_order.py. Existing files are skipped unless --force is given.

Reads --solutions-dir/<student>/<dataset>.json (default results/core/student_solutions) Writes --output-dir/<judge>/<student>_<dataset>_t<budget>.json (default results/judging_protocols/referencefree)
example, from the repository root: python experiments/judging_protocols/run_reference_free.py --judge qwen3-4b --max-tokens 10 8192
experiments/judging_protocols/analyze.py reads the results.

python experiments/judging_protocols/run_reference_free.py --judge JUDGE \

blocks.lead: Generate solutions for the family-bias students with vLLM.

about.html: Same as scripts/run_student.py, but writes to results/family_bias/student_solutions by default. The student is looked up under student_models in slmjury/configs/models.yaml. StudentSolver samples every student the same way (temperature 0.7, top_p 0.9, 1,024 new tokens, no seed), so solutions from different students are comparable. Because sampling is unseeded, regenerating a dataset gives different answers from the ones already judged.

The students vLLM serves are deepseek-r1-0528-qwen3-8b, mistral-7b-v0.3 and qwen3-14b-student. gemma4-31b-student, glm-4.7-flash and qwen3.5-35b-student use architectures that need a newer transformers than vLLM supported; generate them with run_students_hf.py in this folder.
Writes results/family_bias/student_solutions/<student>/<dataset>.json

examples, from the repository root: python experiments/family_bias/run_students.py --student mistral-7b-v0.3 python experiments/family_bias/run_students.py --student qwen3-14b-student --tp 2 --gpu-mem 0.85

blocks.usage:
python experiments/family_bias/run_students.py --student STUDENT \
    [--datasets DATASETS [DATASETS ...]] [--num-samples NUM_SAMPLES] \
    [--output-dir OUTPUT_DIR] [--tensor-parallel-size TENSOR_PARALLEL_SIZE] \
    [--gpu-memory-utilization GPU_MEMORY_UTILIZATION]

actions.help: Student model key from student_models in models.yaml

actions.default: gsm8k gsm_plus math arc_easy arc_challenge hellaswag winogrande truthfulqa

blocks.lead: Generate family-bias student solutions with Hugging Face transformers.

about.html: For students whose architecture the vLLM version used here could not load: gemma4-31b-student (gemma4), glm-4.7-flash (glm4_moe_lite) and qwen3.5-35b-student (qwen3_5_moe). These need transformers 5.x. The model is sharded across all visible GPUs with device_map="auto".

The prompt templates, the routing between them and the answer extraction are the package's own (slmjury.core.solver), and sampling matches StudentSolver.solve_batch: temperature 0.7, top_p 0.9, 1,024 new tokens. The output files have the same fields as the ones run_students.py writes, so the judge step (scripts/run_judge.py) reads them unchanged.
The student is looked up under student_models in slmjury/configs/models.yaml (model, dtype and trust_remote_code are used).
Writes results/family_bias/student_solutions/<student>/<dataset>.json

examples, from the repository root: python experiments/family_bias/run_students_hf.py --student gemma4-31b-student python experiments/family_bias/run_students_hf.py --student qwen3.5-35b-student \ --datasets arc_easy arc_challenge gsm8k winogrande truthfulqa

blocks.usage:
python experiments/family_bias/run_students_hf.py --student STUDENT \
    [--datasets DATASETS [DATASETS ...]] [--num-samples NUM_SAMPLES] \
    [--output-dir OUTPUT_DIR] [--batch-size BATCH_SIZE]
